notes.text: Psalm . This is an individual lament, asking for God’s help against those who threaten the lives of the faithful. The title connects the song to the events of 1 Sam. 23:19, where the Ziphites, among whom David was hiding, promised to hand David over to Saul. The psalm focuses on God’s protection.

The psalm opens by describing the circumstances: ruthless men, who have no respect for God (they do not set God before themselves) seek my life. In such a case the proper appeal is to God’s name (vv. 1, 6; God’s name can be an image for his personal presence).
strangers. The Ziphites, who belong to Judah, are acting like Gentiles in opposing God’s faithful.

The worshiper looks forward to continued enjoyment of God’s presence and favor. The freewill offering is a kind of peace offering (Lev. 7:16), which celebrates God’s goodness with a meal in his presence. The schemes of the ruthless cannot keep the faithful away from God forever.
